description: A capstone practicum in which teams carry an analytics problem for a real or realistic client from scoping to deployment hand-over. Students rehearse every stage in the lab with client scenarios, data pipelines and models, then deliver a final report and a stakeholder presentation.
modelledOn: Provost and Fawcett, Data Science for Business
Sculley et al., Hidden Technical Debt in Machine Learning Systems
Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843) of Ghana and the guidance of the Data Protection Commission
outcomes: Translate a client's business need into a scoped analytics question with success metrics, risks and a project plan.
Assess data access, quality, privacy and ethics requirements and build a documented, lawful data pipeline.
Develop baseline and improved models with leakage-free evaluation designed around the client's costs.
Audit models for subgroup performance, uncertainty and interpretability before recommending action.
Communicate findings to technical and non-technical decision makers in writing and in a live presentation.
Plan deployment hand-over, monitoring and retraining so the client can operate the solution.

units.title: Scoping an analytics problem with a client
topics: Eliciting needs: turning a business question into an analytics question and agreeing what a decision will look like
Success metrics, baselines, feasibility and cost-benefit of the proposed analysis
Project charter, scope boundaries, assumptions, risks and the stakeholder map
Team roles, working agreements and a reproducible repository with version control
Planning the term: work breakdown, Gantt chart, milestones and sprint cadence

units.title: Data access, governance and ethics
topics: Data inventory, data sharing agreements and negotiating access with the data owner
Ghana Data Protection Act principles, lawful basis and consent; anonymisation, pseudonymisation and k-anonymity
Ethics review: risk-benefit assessment, vulnerable groups and community consent
Data quality audit: missingness, collection bias, provenance and a data dictionary
Building the data pipeline in SQL: staging, cleaning, joining and lineage documentation
Secure handling: encryption, access control, audit logs and retention policy

units.title: Exploratory analysis and baseline models
topics: Profiling and exploratory analysis: distributions, segments and sanity checks against domain knowledge
Feature engineering and avoiding target leakage
Baseline models: client heuristics, regression and shallow trees, and the benchmark they set
Evaluation design: temporal and spatial splits and metrics aligned to the client's costs
Mid-project review: presenting early findings and re-scoping with the client

units.title: Iterative modelling and validation
topics: Model iteration: feature sets, tuning, ensembles and a disciplined experiment log
Validation: cross-validation, temporal backtesting and calibration of predicted probabilities
Fairness and subgroup performance audits across region, gender and income group
Error analysis, uncertainty quantification and sensitivity to assumptions
Interpretability for stakeholders: feature importance, partial dependence and case-level explanations
Decision-focused evaluation: cost matrices, expected value and planning an A/B pilot

units.title: Communicating findings to decision makers
topics: Narrative structure for different audiences: board, programme officers and field staff
Visual design for decisions: dashboards, uncertainty displays and avoiding misleading charts
Writing the executive summary and the technical appendix
Handling disagreement and stating limitations without losing credibility

units.title: Deployment hand-over and monitoring
topics: Deployment options: batch scoring, API and dashboard, and fitting into workflows with weak connectivity
Packaging for hand-over: environment capture, containers, documentation and a model card
Monitoring: data drift, performance decay, alerts and retraining triggers
Operating cost, support, runbooks and training of client staff
Post-deployment evaluation and tracking benefits against the original success metrics

units.title: Final report and stakeholder presentation
topics: Structure of the final report: problem, data, methods, results, recommendations and limitations
The reproducibility package: code, data access notes, environment and a one-command rebuild
Presentation rehearsal, anticipating questions and handling live Q&A
Reflection, peer assessment and lessons learned for the next team
Professional practice: reporting negative or inconclusive results honestly

schedule.title: Scoping and planning the engagement
schedule.exercise: Write a two-page project charter for a client brief, covering the question, success metrics, scope, risks, team roles and a milestone plan.

tasks.title: Interview a simulated rural bank manager in a branching scenario, choose which questions to ask and score the resulting problem statement against the rubric
Draw a 13-week Gantt chart with milestones, dependencies and a critical path for a client analytics project
Compute the expected net benefit of a loan default model under three accuracy levels and decide the minimum performance worth building

schedule.title: Data access, privacy and ethics
schedule.exercise: Draft a data sharing agreement and an ethics checklist for a project using patient visit records from a regional health directorate.

tasks.title: Negotiate data access with a hesitant data owner in a case, choose concessions and score the agreement against the rubric
Pseudonymise a customer table with salted hashes and generalise ages and districts until the table is 5-anonymous, then verify it with a query
Review a proposed survey of schoolchildren in a case, identify the ethical risks, set consent rules and defend your decisions

schedule.title: Data quality and the pipeline
schedule.exercise: Document a data dictionary and lineage diagram for a pipeline that joins mobile-money transactions, customer records and agent locations.

tasks.title: Profile a messy transactions table with SQL, count nulls, duplicates and impossible values and write the data quality report
Build a staging, cleaning and mart pipeline in SQL for three source tables and test it with row-count reconciliation checks
Apply file permissions, an encrypted archive and an access log to a project data folder and demonstrate that an unauthorised user is blocked

schedule.title: Exploration, features and baselines
schedule.exercise: Present three exploratory findings with one chart each and, for each, say whether the client can act on it and what you would check next.

tasks.title: Profile a clinic visit dataset in Python, plot distributions by district and list five questions to take back to the client
Find and remove a leaking feature from a loan default dataset and show how the validation score drops to a realistic value
Build the client's current rule as a baseline, then a logistic regression and a small tree, and report the gain over the rule

schedule.title: Evaluation design and mid-project review
schedule.exercise: Prepare and rehearse a ten-minute mid-project review that states what has been learned, what has changed in scope and what decision you need from the client.

tasks.title: Design a time-based split for a monthly sales forecast, compare it with a random split and show the optimism of the random split
Choose a threshold for a fraud alert model by minimising a cost matrix supplied by the client and plot cost against threshold
Handle a mid-project review in which the client changes the goal, decide what to descope and score your response against the rubric

schedule.title: Modelling iterations and validation
schedule.exercise: Keep an experiment log of at least eight modelling runs with the hypothesis, change, result and decision for each.

tasks.title: Run a grid of eight feature sets and models for a crop-yield task and record each result in an experiment log table
Backtest a model over six rolling monthly windows and report how performance varies from window to window
Check the calibration of predicted default probabilities with a reliability plot and apply isotonic recalibration to fix them

schedule.title: Fairness, errors and uncertainty
schedule.exercise: Write an audit note on whether a credit model performs equally for women and men, urban and rural customers, and propose a response to any gap.

tasks.title: Compute recall and false-positive rate by region and gender for a classifier and flag gaps larger than five percentage points
Build bootstrap intervals for the headline metric and test how the result changes under three different missing-data assumptions
Decide in a case what to do when a model is accurate overall but fails for one district, and score your decision against the rubric

schedule.title: Interpretation and decisions
schedule.exercise: Explain your best model to a district officer in one page without technical terms, and give the decision rule you recommend.

tasks.title: Compute permutation importance and partial dependence for a health facility model and write the plain-language reading of the top three drivers
Compute the expected value of acting on the model scores with the cost matrix and compare with the client's current policy
Plan an A/B pilot by calculating sample size and power needed to detect a five percent improvement in repayment

schedule.title: Communicating findings
schedule.exercise: Produce a one-page executive summary and a three-slide outline for the board, then revise them after peer feedback.

tasks.title: Choose the story structure for a board briefing in a case and score the draft against an audience-fit rubric
Redraw a misleading chart with a truncated axis and hidden uncertainty into an honest one and list each change
Respond to a hostile question about model limits in a stakeholder meeting case and score your reply against the rubric

schedule.title: Deployment and packaging
schedule.exercise: Choose a deployment option for a client with weak connectivity and no data engineers, and write the hand-over checklist that supports it.

tasks.title: Pick a deployment option for a district health office with weak connectivity in a case and score the trade-offs against the rubric
Package a scoring script with pinned dependencies and a container build file, run it from a clean machine and write the README
Detect data drift in monthly feature distributions with a population stability index and set an alert threshold that avoids false alarms

schedule.title: Operations, handover and benefits tracking
schedule.exercise: Write a runbook that lets the client's staff retrain the model, check its health and roll back a bad release.

tasks.title: Draw a monitoring and retraining flow diagram showing triggers, owners and escalation for the client's scoring service
Cost one year of running the model, including compute, staff time and retraining, and compare it with the benefit estimate
Track a benefit metric before and after launch with a simple difference-in-differences against a comparison group and report the effect

schedule.title: Final report and reproducibility
schedule.exercise: Submit the full draft final report with a reproducibility package that a peer team can rebuild with a single command.

tasks.title: Assemble the sections of a final report in a case, order them for the client, and score the structure against the rubric
Build a one-command script that recreates the results from raw data in a fresh environment and checks the output hash
Decide how to report an inconclusive result to a client who hoped for a positive finding, and score your decision against the rubric

schedule.title: Presentation and reflection
schedule.exercise: Deliver a fifteen-minute stakeholder presentation followed by questions, and complete a reflection and peer assessment.

tasks.title: Rehearse a stakeholder presentation in a case with three audience types, choose what to cut and score the plan against the rubric
Answer ten likely questions in a mock Q&A, deciding for each what to admit, what to defer and what to show
Write a structured reflection on a team conflict case, identify what went wrong and score your lessons against the rubric
